coverage: Pier & Point covers four sites on San Francisco's central waterfront: Mission Rock, Mission Bay, Pier 70 and Potrero Power Station. A parcel that is not in this data is outside coverage, not "no activity".

record.name: Building 12 Plaza and Market Square
record.summary: The roughly 1.5-acre 'social centerpiece' of the Pier 70 open-space network (D4D Section 3.9): Market Square between Buildings 2 and 12 and Parcel D, the Building 12 entry plaza on 22nd Street, a Maryland Street platform for vendors and food trucks, and possibly the retained structural frame of Building 15. Building 12 itself reopened in 2022 and Maryland Street's paving is done, but the plaza is a Phase 1 park still tied to adjacent vertical development.

notes.accuracy_caveat: The outline is the union of Assessor lots 4114008 and 4114004, so its edges are recorded lot lines, not a trace. The lot choice was made by the owner on a reading of the diagram and the satellite imagery; no document read ties these lots to the plaza. The lots do not cover all of the open ground the D4D draws around Buildings 2 and 12, so the earlier outline's extent is not reproduced. A building may sit back from the lot lines. The plaza is planned (Port Item 11A, memo dated Aug 7, 2026: the balance of Phase 1, largely the Phase 1 parks and open space, will be built on a schedule that coincides with adjacent vertical development).
notes.digitized_from: DataSF Assessor parcels (acdm-wktn), lots 4114008 and 4114004 (recorded 2019-02-07, 2020-10-23; mapped 2019-03-14, 2021-07-07; active), joined into one outline; cross-checked against Pier 70 Design for Development Figure 6.4.2 - Building Height Maximum (p.155).
notes.why_no_real_parcel: The outline is the union of Assessor lots 4114008 and 4114004 (active), chosen by the owner as the lots under the plaza; no document names them as the plaza.
notes.regulatory_context: Part of the Pier 70 D4D's Open Space Network (Section 3.9), approximately 1.5 acres. Per Section 3.9, Market Square lies north of Building 12 (between Building 2 and Parcel D, entered from 21st St), the Building 12 Entry Plaza south of Building 12 on 22nd St, and the Maryland Street Platform along Building 12's Maryland St side; the mapped block spans Louisiana St to Maryland St.

facts.value: 3.9 'Building 12 Plaza and Market Square', zone 5 of Figure 3.4.1

Market Square (flanked by rehabilitated buildings and new construction on three sides, four access ways, a compact tree grove), Building 12 Entry Plaza south of Building 12 on 22nd Street, Maryland Street Platform, and the Building 15 structural frame pending a structural feasibility study
A pedestrian opening on 21st Street between Building 2 and Parcel D; the existing passageway through Buildings 2 and 12; a Building 12 entrance from 22nd Street; a direct entry from Maryland Street
Open-air markets, community gatherings, small performances; Market Square extends Maryland Street with coordinated paving to accommodate vendors and food trucks

Within the Phase 1 area (Port's 2026 Exhibit A); Port Item 9B (2017, Table A) lists Building 12 Plaza (OS-1) and Market Square (OS-2) among the Phase 1 parks, and Port Item 11A cites three acres of Phase 1 parks overall

changes.text: Pier 70 Building 12 Plaza now uses real Assessor lot lines.

The 2042 date on this record was drawn as an expected completion. The Port's 2017 staff report calls it an outside date in the Development Agreement's Schedule of Performance (Phase 3 within approximately 25 years of approval), not a construction schedule. It is now labelled a legal deadline and no longer moves this record's status on the map or the timeline.

The plaza's layout is now described as the D4D gives it (Market Square north of Building 12, the entry plaza south, the Maryland Street Platform on its east side), and the map notes no longer claim the site was never subdivided by the Assessor or explain the acreage gap as a fact. The 2042 completion milestone is now a soft placeholder (the 2017 Phase 3 outside date, tolled by down market delay) rather than a forecast, and the Building 15 move is dated to the 2018-2020 window the Port gives. Image credits no longer name design firms the figure does not credit or say 'adopted 2017', and Phase 1 park membership is cited to Port Item 9B.

open_questions: No Port Commission schematic design approval or construction record for Market Square or the entry plaza was found; the interim events documented by the Port took place inside Building 12 and under Building 15, not on a finished plaza.

Whether the Building 15 structural frame is being retained (the D4D marks it 'pending structural feasibility study'): the Port's June 2025 deck shows Building 15 relocated over 22nd Street but does not say what will remain of it.

No openly licensed or public-record post-rehabilitation photo of Building 12 was found (checked Wikimedia Commons -- geosearch, category and title search all came up empty for anything dated 2022 or later). Perkins&Will's Building 12 wayfinding photography (by Bruce Damonte, via DNCO's case study) and Pier 70's own project photography are copyrighted, but their press/media contacts may grant editorial, non-commercial clearance on request -- worth revisiting if someone follows up with them.
